children: According to Sina Finance, Goldman Sachs said continued central-bank gold purchases would give gold support that silver lacks, even as Federal Reserve rate hikes weigh on private investors’ demand for both metals. The bank forecasts gold at $4,650 per ounce at the end of 2027 and $5,600 per ounce at the end of 2028 after the Fed resumes rate cuts.

Goldman economists expect the Fed to raise rates by 25 basis points in December and again in March 2027. The bank forecasts global central banks will buy about 60 tons of gold per month from 2026 through 2028, compared with an average of 17 tons per month before 2022. On a seasonally adjusted three-month moving-average basis, purchases fell to 51 tons in September from 85 tons in August, but Goldman said demand had likely recovered as gold prices stabilized.

Goldman estimates that its end-2027 gold target is about 13% above the average price of $4,100 per ounce in October. It forecasts a price of $4,585 at the end of 2027 if the Fed makes four cumulative rate hikes and reaches a higher terminal rate, and $4,265 if that scenario is combined with gold funds selling 300 tons.

Silver briefly topped $120 per ounce earlier this year amid tight liquidity in London. Goldman said concerns in 2025 about possible U.S. tariffs on silver contributed to outflows from London, reducing local inventories, while stronger investment demand tightened spot supply. Under normal conditions, an additional 1,000 tons of net silver demand per week typically raises prices by about 2%; during the earlier supply squeeze, the increase was about 7%. Goldman expects Fed rate hikes to curb silver ETF demand and says silver is unlikely to repeat that squeeze. It also does not view the gold-silver ratio’s return to the upper end of its historical range as a sign that silver is about to outperform gold.

Goldman forecasts four 25-basis-point Fed rate cuts from November 2027 through September 2028. It said renewed demand from Western gold funds would support gold, while silver could also benefit from a recovery in investment demand. The bank warned that a further rise in international oil prices could prompt more systematic selling by CTA funds, adding pressure on gold.

title: Goldman Sachs: Gold to Outperform Silver and Reach $5,600 by End-2028
